title: Relative functor equivalence over an ordinary base
statement:
Use coherent functor quasicategories and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], and isofibrations of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Let $S=N(J)$ for a small ordinary category $J$ whose only isomorphisms are identities. Let $P$ be a small simplicial set, $M$ a small quasicategory, and $i:P\to M$ a categorical equivalence equipped with structure maps $s_M:M\to S$ and $s_P=s_Mi$. Let $p:V\to S$ be an isofibration of quasicategories; $V$ need not be small, and all functor simplicial sets are formed in a universe containing $V$. Define
$$\operatorname{Fun}_S(T,V)=\operatorname{Fun}(T,V)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(T,S)}\{s_T\}\qquad(T=P,M).$$
These are quasicategories and restriction induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Fun}_S(M,V)\to\operatorname{Fun}_S(P,V)$. For two objects $F,G$ of either relative functor category, its mapping space is naturally equivalent to the homotopy fiber at the identity transformation of $s_T$ of
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(T,V)}(F,G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(T,S)}(s_T,s_T).$$
These mapping-space identifications are compatible with restriction along $i$, and all assertions are natural in functors over $S$ and in all coherent transformation parameters. Homotopy fiber has the path-space meaning of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Remark A.4.2, comparison over the operadic base; strict-fiber convention. Online source; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Work in one universe containing $V$, $S$, and the small indexing sets. For any small $T\to S$, put $C_T=\operatorname{Fun}(T,V)$, $D_T=\operatorname{Fun}(T,S)$ and $E_T=C_T\times_{D_T}\{s_T\}$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow T$: $C_T\to D_T$ is an isofibration between quasicategories. Every inner-horn problem in $E_T$ is precisely an inner-horn problem in $C_T$ above the constant simplex at $s_T$; its filler therefore remains in $E_T$. Thus $E_T$ is a quasicategory, including when it is empty. This applies to $P,M$ and the intermediate $Q$ below.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.1 (Kerodon tag 01F1), applied with empty A; pullback lifting written explicitly.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], $i$ is a Joyal weak equivalence. Factor it by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] as $P\xrightarrow{j}Q\xrightarrow{q}M$, with $j$ a trivial cofibration and $q$ a fibration. Two-out-of-three makes $q$ a trivial fibration, so it lifts every degreewise injective map. Give $Q$ the structure map $s_Q=s_Mq$. Since $M$ is fibrant, composing $q$ with $M\to *$ shows that $Q$ is fibrant and hence a quasicategory. Explicitly, any lifting problem for this composite is solved first in $M$ and then against $q$. By [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations], the given isofibration $p:V\to S$ is a Joyal fibration. No quasicategory hypothesis on $P$ is used.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and Proposition 2.2.5.8; agent application of the model factorizations over S.

proof.text: We show directly that $j^*:E_Q\to E_P$ lifts every degreewise injective $a:A\hookrightarrow B$. A square for this map is, by the internal-Hom formula, exactly the extension problem against $p$ for the prescribed map on $(Q\times A)\amalg_{P\times A}(P\times B)$, above $Q\times B\to Q\to S$. Its inclusion into $Q\times B$ is the pushout-product $j\square a$. By [lem-coef-joyal-cartesian-pushout-product] it is a trivial cofibration. The fibration property of $p$ gives the desired filler with the specified base map. Thus $j^*$ is a trivial fibration by the weak factorization system in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Its source and target are quasicategories by step 1, so [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations](2) makes this specified restriction a coherent functor equivalence.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4 and Theorem 2.2.5.1; the relative exponential lifting square is written out.

proof.text: The lifting property of $q$ against $\varnothing\hookrightarrow M$ gives a section $t:M\to Q$ with $qt=\mathrm{id}_M$. Let $L$ be the nerve of the groupoid with two objects and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair, as in [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval]. Lift against the degreewise injective inclusion $Q\times\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow Q\times L$, prescribing $\mathrm{id}_Q$ and $tq$ at the endpoints and prescribing $q\operatorname{pr}_Q$ in $M$. This gives $H:Q\times L\to Q$ over $M$. Precomposition with $t$ is an inverse to $q^*:E_M\to E_Q$: one composite is exactly the identity, and precomposition with $H$ gives a coherent equivalence from the other to the identity. Indeed the reverse edge and the two inverse triangles of $L$ supply its inverse and both triangle witnesses after evaluation in $V$. The equation $qH=q\operatorname{pr}_Q$ ensures that every parameter remains strictly over $S$. Consequently $q^*$ is an equivalence and $i^*=j^*q^*$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Remark A.4.2, categorical-equivalence replacement; agent proof by the model lifting properties and the walking-isomorphism nerve.

proof.text: Fix $T=P$ or $M$ and $F,G\in E_T$. For a quasicategory $B$, write $U_B(x,y)=\{x\}\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B}\{y\}$. Unpacking the degreewise pullbacks gives the exact equality $U_{E_T}(F,G)=U_{C_T}(F,G)\times_{U_{D_T}(s_T,s_T)}\{\mathrm{id}_{s_T}\}$. Here the identity means the constant arrow and all its degeneracies. By the final assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], the map $U_{C_T}(F,G)\to U_{D_T}(s_T,s_T)$ is a Kan fibration of Kan complexes, since $C_T\to D_T$ is an inner fibration. By [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], inserting the constant path identifies the displayed strict fiber with the path-space homotopy fiber up to weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.1.22 (01P8) and Proposition 3.4.0.7 (0329); these are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Apply the natural right-pinch equivalences of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] to $E_T,C_T,D_T$. They take the identity vertex in $\operatorname{Map}_{D_T}(s_T,s_T)$ to the identity vertex in $U_{D_T}(s_T,s_T)$. Thus [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance], with the third factor the one-point space, compares their path-space homotopy fibers. Combining this with step 5 gives the natural zigzag of weak equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{E_T}(F,G)\to U_{E_T}(F,G)\to\operatorname{hofib}_{\mathrm{id}}(U_{C_T}(F,G)\to U_{D_T}(s_T,s_T))\leftarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{\mathrm{id}}(\operatorname{Map}_{C_T}(F,G)\to\operatorname{Map}_{D_T}(s_T,s_T))$. This proves precisely the asserted mapping-space equivalence using the right-pinched convention; it does not assume that the right-pinched map itself is a Kan fibration.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5) and Proposition 3.4.0.9 (032B), applied to the natural pinch square.

proof.text: Every arrow of the zigzag in step 6 is given by restriction, evaluation, the pinch map, or insertion of a constant path. For restriction along $i$, the equations $(pF)i=p(Fi)$ and $(pG)i=p(Gi)$ make the two mapping-space squares commute; the identity vertex restricts to the identity vertex. The same equations hold degree by degree for a functor $V\to V\prime$ over $S$, whenever both targets satisfy the hypotheses. Pinching a parameterized simplex and then restricting is the same map as restricting and then pinching, since both are precomposition with the same product map. Inserting a constant path also commutes exactly with these operations. Thus the entire zigzag is compatible with restriction and postcomposition, with all coherent transformation parameters retained. The restriction equivalence of steps 1-4 is the specified simplicial map $i^*$, which has the same strict naturality. No natural choice of the auxiliary section or of an inverse functor is being asserted.

source.place: Naturality of the pinch maps and the degreewise internal-Hom and path-space formulas; direct parameter check.

proof_origin.place: Remark A.4.2 motivates the over-base comparison; the argument here expands it using the cited Joyal and mapping-space tools.
